title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DEE'S TREEHOUSE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Dee Fontaine, a bank loan officer from Chattanooga, Tennessee.
When Dee was eight, her big brothers built a treehouse and nailed up a sign: No Girls Allowed.
Forty-seven years later, she still wasn't over it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: SOMEDAY
segments.quote: The sure conviction that we could if we wanted to is the reason so many good minds are idle.
segments.author: Georg Christoph Lichtenberg
lines: For years Dee said, I could build my own treehouse, if I wanted to.
One slow Monday, she opened a book of sayings by Lichtenberg, an old German professor:
The sure conviction that we could if we wanted to is the reason so many good minds are idle.
Dee shut the book. That night she bought a hammer, two hundred nails and a how-to book.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LADDER
segments.author: Desiderius Erasmus
lines: On day one, she climbed the old oak with a board under each arm. The ladder wobbled. So did Dee.
Her neighbor Walt, a retired lineman, shouted up a saying Erasmus wrote down five hundred years ago:
Prevention is better than cure.
So she bought a harness and a helmet. She looked like an astronaut picking pecans. But she never fell.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE SHORT BOARDS
segments.author: Old carpenters' saying
lines: Then she cut six floor boards. All six were four inches too short.
The man at the lumber yard grinned and tapped the old sign over his saw:
Measure twice, cut once.
Dee measured twice. Some days three times. The short boards became a very nice bench.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE HEAVY PART
segments.quote: All things excellent are as difficult as they are rare.
segments.author: Baruch Spinoza
lines: By August her arms hurt, the walls were crooked, and the mosquitoes knew her by name.
She almost quit. Then she found a line she had taped to her toolbox, from the Dutch thinker Spinoza:
All things excellent are as difficult as they are rare.
Hard meant worth it. She raised the roof that Saturday, one sweaty board at a time.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BROTHERS
segments.quote: Never cut what you can untie.
segments.author: Joseph Joubert
lines: Her brothers, Ricky and Joe, drove by and laughed. Ricky said, Need a permit, Sis?
She wanted to put up her own sign: No Brothers Allowed.
But Mom always quoted Joubert, a French writer:
Never cut what you can untie.
So Dee handed them each a hammer. They worked all weekend, told old stories, and nobody stayed mad.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE NEW SIGN
segments.quote: Whoever is happy will make others happy too.
segments.author: Anne Frank
lines: In October, Dee sat up in the oak with coffee, watching the sunset over the river.
She felt so happy she remembered a line from Anne Frank's diary:
Whoever is happy will make others happy too.
So she painted a new sign: Everybody Allowed. Now the whole street comes up for coffee on Sundays.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Stop saying someday. Be careful. Measure twice. Push through. Untie the knot. Share the view.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Stop saying someday. Be careful. Measure twice. Push through the hard part. Untie the knot. Share the view.
I'd visit Dee's treehouse, but the last time I climbed a ladder, the fire department had to help.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
